audit_target: Public N-only, factor-blind state/process semantics not representable by a fixed finite ring term, capable of creating one-sided hidden-CRT behavior while every declared scalar projection before the selective-collapse layer remains gcd-clean (gcd 1 or N).

parent_firewall.accepted_boundary: Fixed finite-step polynomial/localized-ring semantics are N-erased modulo N; one-sided rank loss is fixed determinantal support and exposes its factor by gcd.
parent_firewall.audit_question: Do established non-ring/stateful factoring mechanisms exactly duplicate the surviving guarded class, or only antecede it through excluded order, collision, congruence-of-squares, known-prime p-adic, or direct-nonunit mechanisms?

policy: Classification is hypothesis-by-hypothesis, not name similarity.
NO_MATERIAL_MATCH and NO_EXACT_DUPLICATE_FOUND are search boundaries, never novelty evidence.

A method is not an exact duplicate if its selective event is already an excluded order/smoothness, collision, congruence-of-squares/relation, known-prime p-adic, or direct scalar nonunit/gcd mechanism.
Distinguish per-step CRT product naturality from process-level stopping/history asymmetry.

sources.citation: J. M. Pollard, Theorems on factorization and primality testing, Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 76(3) (1974), 521-528.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N, public base c coprime to N, and a public smoothness/exponent schedule M.
sources.hidden_information_assumptions: No factor is supplied, but success depends on one hidden p having p-1 dividing/sufficiently dividing the public exponent schedule.
sources.evolving_state: Repeated modular exponentiation / accumulation of a large smooth exponent.
sources.selective_collapse_event: c^M becomes 1 modulo one hidden factor before it becomes 1 modulo all hidden factors.
sources.guard_relation: Excluded by the task's Pollard/order-annihilation/smoothness guard. It demonstrates process-level hidden-channel asymmetry, not a surviving new primitive.

sources.citation: H. C. Williams, A p+1 method of factoring, Mathematics of Computation 39(159) (1982), 225-234.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N plus public Lucas-sequence parameters and a smoothness schedule.
sources.hidden_information_assumptions: No factor is supplied; success is tied to one hidden p for which p+1 (or the relevant Lucas-group order) is smooth.
sources.evolving_state: Lucas-sequence / algebraic-group state modulo N under a large smooth index.
sources.stopping_predicate: A scheduled nonunit/gcd test on the Lucas-state expression.
sources.selective_collapse_event: The relevant group state reaches its distinguished identity/trace condition modulo one hidden factor only.

sources.citation: H. W. Lenstra Jr., Factoring integers with elliptic curves, Annals of Mathematics 126(3) (1987), 649-673.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N, a public/random elliptic curve and point, and public scalar-multiplication smoothness bounds.
sources.hidden_information_assumptions: No factor is supplied; success depends on the order of the reduction of the chosen curve/point modulo one hidden prime factor.
sources.evolving_state: Elliptic-curve scalar-multiplication state over Z/NZ (typically projective coordinates).
sources.stopping_predicate: A noninvertible coordinate/denominator or projective coordinate whose gcd with N is proper.
sources.selective_collapse_event: A smooth scalar kills the point modulo one hidden curve group but not the other.
sources.final_factor_extraction: A gcd of the nonunit coordinate/denominator with N.
sources.guard_relation: A particularly close geometric antecedent, but still an algebraic-group order/smoothness mechanism explicitly guarded out by the task.

sources.citation: J. M. Pollard, A Monte Carlo method for factorization, BIT 15(3) (1975), 331-334.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N, a public polynomial map and seed.
sources.hidden_information_assumptions: No factor is supplied; the same recurrence modulo hidden p and q has different cycle/collision times.
sources.evolving_state: History of iterates x_i modulo N plus a collision-detection schedule.
sources.stopping_predicate: gcd(x_i-x_j,N) (or batched product differences) becomes proper.
sources.selective_collapse_event: A pair of iterates collides modulo one hidden factor before the other.
sources.guard_relation: Excluded by the rho/collision guard. Important distinction: every fixed update is CRT-natural; the escape from the parent fixed-grammar theorem is the unbounded/history-dependent event search.

sources.citation: M. A. Morrison and J. Brillhart, A method of factoring and the factorization of F_7, Mathematics of Computation 29 (1975), 183-205.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N and the continued-fraction expansion data of sqrt(kN) or a related public quadratic irrational.
sources.evolving_state: Continued-fraction convergents, canonical quotient/floor state, and accumulated smooth relations.
sources.stopping_predicate: Enough relations exist to form a square relation / congruence of squares modulo N.
sources.selective_collapse_event: A global relation produces X^2 congruent Y^2 mod N with X not congruent +/-Y on all hidden channels.
sources.guard_relation: Covers the Euclidean/continued-fraction and canonical quotient/floor classes, but is excluded by the congruence-of-squares guard.

sources.citation: C. Pomerance, The Quadratic Sieve Factoring Algorithm, EUROCRYPT 1984; J. D. Dixon, Asymptotically fast factorization of integers, Mathematics of Computation 36 (1981), 255-260.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N, public factor base / sieve interval / random residues.
sources.evolving_state: Collection of smooth residues and parity vectors followed by linear algebra modulo 2.
sources.stopping_predicate: A nontrivial parity dependency yields a congruence of squares.
sources.selective_collapse_event: The two square roots agree up to sign differently on hidden CRT channels.
sources.guard_relation: History/relation and modular-linear-algebra antecedent, but the final mechanism is exactly the excluded congruence-of-squares family.

sources.citation: Ordinary Number Field Sieve background exposition following the standard NFS relation-collection, F_2 linear-algebra and square-root stages.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N plus public polynomial selection, smoothness bounds and relation search.
sources.evolving_state: Large relation history; sparse exponent-parity matrix; kernel vectors; square-root reconstruction.
sources.stopping_predicate: A matrix dependency survives the square-root stage and gives a nontrivial congruence of squares.
sources.selective_collapse_event: The reconstructed square roots have different sign pairing on hidden CRT channels.
sources.final_factor_extraction: A gcd of the square-root difference/sum with N.
sources.guard_relation: Strong lattice/relation/modular-linear-algebra antecedent; excluded because it terminates in congruence-of-squares factor extraction.

sources.citation: R. S. Lehman, Factoring Large Integers, Mathematics of Computation 28 (1974), 637-646; W. B. Hart, A One Line Factoring Algorithm, Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society 92(1) (2012), 61-69.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N plus public search multipliers/intervals.
sources.evolving_state: Canonical floor/ceiling square-root and difference-of-squares search state.
sources.stopping_predicate: A tested difference becomes an exact square.
sources.final_factor_extraction: gcd(a-b,N), or direct division from a±b when k=1.
sources.guard_relation: Covers canonical representative/floor state but remains Fermat/difference-of-squares and is excluded by the congruence-of-squares guard.

sources.citation: Hensel lifting: simple roots/factorizations modulo a prime p lift to higher powers p^k; standard p-adic lifting interface.
sources.public_inputs: A prime p (or an explicitly supplied maximal ideal) and a root/factorization modulo p.
sources.hidden_information_assumptions: The p-adic place is already named; in the N=pq factoring target this would supply precisely the hidden channel that the task forbids naming.
sources.stopping_predicate: Precision/lift target achieved or a p-adic condition fails.
sources.selective_collapse_event: Valuation behavior occurs in a specified p-adic channel.
sources.final_factor_extraction: Not an N-only hidden-factor discovery in the standard Hensel interface.
sources.guard_relation: Useful non-ring/valuation state, but not factor-blind N-only because the relevant prime/maximal ideal is an input.

sources.citation: M. O. Rabin, Digitalized Signatures and Public-Key Functions as Intractable as Factorization, MIT/LCS/TR-212 (1979); standard reduction from nontrivial modular square roots to factoring.
sources.public_inputs: Composite N=pq and an oracle/process producing a square root not tied to the originally chosen sign pair.
sources.hidden_information_assumptions: No factor need be supplied to the root oracle, but a nontrivial square root of unity already encodes opposite signs on the hidden CRT channels.
sources.stopping_predicate: Obtain a nontrivial square root of unity gamma != +/-1.
sources.selective_collapse_event: gamma is +1 on one hidden factor and -1 on the other.
sources.guard_relation: Exact endpoint equivalence: once the scalar witness is present, the hidden factor is already exposed by gcd. It therefore cannot satisfy the pre-collapse scalar-clean firewall unless this witness itself is declared to be the collapse layer.

sources.citation: Elementary CRT classification of idempotents in Z/nZ; for n with multiple prime-power components, idempotents correspond to 0/1 choices on each CRT component.
sources.public_inputs: A scalar residue e or z modulo composite N.
sources.hidden_information_assumptions: No factor is needed to verify idempotence/nonunit status, but constructing a nontrivial CRT idempotent generally encodes a decomposition.
sources.evolving_state: Not a distinct algorithmic process; algebraic witness class.
sources.stopping_predicate: e^2=e with e not in {0,1}, or a scalar z becomes a proper zero divisor/nonunit.
sources.selective_collapse_event: The scalar is 0 on at least one but not all hidden CRT components (or e is 0/1 with different choices).
sources.final_factor_extraction: For N=pq, proper scalar nonunit z gives gcd(z,N)=p or q; nontrivial idempotent e gives complementary gcd(e,N) and gcd(e-1,N).
sources.guard_relation: This is the algebraic endpoint boundary itself, not a surviving pre-collapse mechanism.

sources.citation: Targeted searches for factorization methods whose decisive mechanism is only canonical representative / quotient-remainder / carry state, without order, collision, square-relation, named p-adic place, or direct nonunit exposure.
sources.evolving_state: Would be canonical representative, quotient/remainder or carry history not reducible to fixed ring terms.
sources.stopping_predicate: Would need a support-faithful one-sided hidden-channel event with all earlier scalar projections gcd-clean.
sources.selective_collapse_event: No established exact match located under the simultaneous guards.
sources.guard_relation: Search boundary only. Existing quotient/floor examples located in CFRAC/QS/Fermat/Lehman/Hart collapse into the excluded congruence-of-squares family.

mechanism_level_synthesis.per_step_crt_naturality: Pollard rho and modular exponentiation examples show that the arithmetic update can remain exactly CRT-natural at every fixed step.
mechanism_level_synthesis.process_level_escape: Classical algorithms escape the parent's fixed finite grammar through variable-time/event searches, changing support schedules, random curves, collision history, relation accumulation, or a supplied p-adic place.
mechanism_level_synthesis.scalar_firewall: For N=pq, any scalar s that is zero modulo exactly one hidden factor immediately exposes that factor as gcd(s,N). Likewise nontrivial CRT idempotents and square roots of unity expose factors by gcd.
mechanism_level_synthesis.surviving_guarded_residue: Any materially distinct successor must keep the asymmetric information typed/non-scalar until the declared collapse layer and must not reduce to order/smoothness, collision, congruence-of-squares/relation, named-prime p-adic, or direct scalar nonunit extraction.

required_joint_features: state/process not representable by one fixed finite polynomial/localized-ring term
every declared scalar projection before the collapse layer has gcd 1 or N with N
not Pollard/Williams/ECM group-order or smoothness annihilation
not congruence-of-squares / Fermat / CFRAC / QS / Dixon / NFS relation factoring
not a p-adic/Hensel process with the hidden prime/maximal ideal already supplied
not merely construction/discovery of a scalar zero divisor, nonunit, idempotent or nontrivial square root whose gcd already factors N
